summary.headline: Ather Energy Q2 FY27: wholesale volume up 42% YoY to 93,000 units, first positive PAT, and gross margin at 24% (H1 FY27: 23%).
summary.overview: Management reported strong demand with preorders up about 108% and inquiries up about 109% YoY, supporting wholesale volume of 93,000 units (up 42% YoY) and registrations of about 92,500 (up nearly 60%). Average ex-showroom price rose to INR164,000 from INR150,000 in Q4 FY26, and adjusted gross margin reached 24% in Q2 FY27 versus 25.4% in Q4 FY26 after commodity headwinds. EBITDA turned positive at 4.9% (from -9.6% a year earlier) and the company reported its first positive PAT. Management is raising installed capacity to 11.4 lakh units per year by Q2 FY28 because demand exceeds supply, and Konarc launched in phases from late August.

segments.name: Zones (registrations growth)
segments.commentary: Industry registrations grew 82% YoY to about 6 lakh in Q2. Ather growth was 82% in South, 85% in Middle India and 79% in Rest of India; Rest of India was the fastest-rising zone as Konarc rolled out in northern states and sales were prioritised there.

segments.name: Konarc (new mainstream scooter)
segments.commentary: Launched 29 August 2026 with only one month of sales in Q2 and fewer than 10,000 units sold by quarter-end. Mid variants SR2 and SR3 are live, SR1 is due by Q4 FY27, and the Z variant is not yet in production.

segments.name: Non-vehicle revenue
segments.commentary: Non-vehicle revenue was 15% of total. AtherStack Pro is more than 50% of it, with accessories and servicing split roughly equally. Management indicated gross margins of about 30-40% for accessories, 40-45% for spares and 80-90% for AtherStack Pro.

guidance_outlook: Installed capacity to rise from 9.2 lakh units/year to 11.4 lakh units/year by Q2 FY28, through Hosur (+6,000 units/month, live later this quarter) and AURIC Phase 1 (base 42,000 units/month, plus 12,000 units/month incremental).

AURIC Phase 1 trial production expected in the next few weeks (Q3 FY27), with capex installation complete by Q4 FY27; full capacity realisation takes a couple of quarters, with ramp-up expected within FY28.
Dealer/experience-centre network expansion to restart from around end of Q3 FY27, with noticeable numbers from Q4 FY27; fewer than 50 experience centres were added in the last two quarters.

No further price hikes in Q3 FY27 and no planned price increases on the current portfolio for the next few quarters; Konarc's entry variants may lower average ex-showroom price without hurting gross margin.
Management expects like-to-like Konarc gross margin to be 6-7% better than Rizta in the long term; Konarc is already a few thousand rupees cheaper than Rizta on a like-to-like basis.
Commodities seen as flat in recent weeks; management says Q3 is not expected to be worse than Q2 but volatility remains high. Subsidy is broadly unchanged QoQ.
Electric motorcycle launch: no timeline given.
capex_capacity: Current manufacturing capacity averaged 33,000 units/month in Q2 FY27, up from 28,000 in Q1; Hosur is at 35,000 units/month capacity and is described as at its limit.
Hosur expansion adds 6,000 units/month, live later in Q3 FY27. Total installed capacity is about 77,000 units/month after AURIC Phase 1 base (42,000) before the additional expansion.
AURIC Phase 1 (Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar) adds 12,000 units/month of incremental capacity by Q2 FY28, taking installed capacity to 11.4 lakh units/year from 9.2 lakh units/year.
Management estimates about 20,000 units/month of unrealised retail demand at current run-rate, with demand in the 50,000-60,000 units/month range.
Ather Node (apartment EV charging) is being industrialised and will begin deployment in the next few months; Ather Bedrock 5th-gen battery packs are live across 450, Rizta and Konarc.
demand_pricing: Preorders rose about 108% YoY to about 1.8 lakh; inquiries rose about 109% YoY to over 10 lakh; Ather searches rose about 94% vs about 34% for EV searches industry-wide.
Pan-India E2W penetration crossed 10% for the first time, at about 11.2% for Q2 FY27 (industry commentary cites 11.6% as the quarterly figure).
Average ex-showroom price rose to INR164,000 from INR150,000 in Q4 FY26, helped by price hikes and SKU/incentive management. Management says part of the gain is temporary.
Commodity inflation (aluminium, copper, plastics, memory chips) hit gross margin by about 9.4%. Management says SKU management recovered 2.7pp of this, a more temporary lever.
Structural gross-margin gains of about 5.3pp over two quarters came from price hikes, VAVE and cost reduction.
Konarc early Stack Pro attach rates are said to be as strong as Rizta, but management wants at least two quarters before assuming ~90% attach for Konarc, given a more non-South-heavy mix.
Tier 2 penetration is rising fastest; Maharashtra Tier 2 penetration is about 18-19%. Company is not yet present in rural markets.

qa_highlights.question: How quickly will the new AURIC Phase 1 capacity ramp up, given it is greenfield, and when will the 6.5 lakh figure be realised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AURIC Phase 1's base 42,000 units will take about two quarters to ramp; the additional 12,000 units going live in Q2 FY28 may ramp faster. Full ramp is expected within FY28, while Hosur ramp is expected to be rapid from the end of Q3.

qa_highlights.question: How much pricing headroom remains if commodities stay elevated into next calendar year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not want to raise prices on the current portfolio for the next few quarters. Konarc's more aggressive entry portfolio gives better unit economics, so it could lower average ex-showroom price without hurting gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: How are Konarc bookings and cannibalisation trending in launched regions?
qa_highlights.answer: Konarc has only one month of sales in Q2 and fewer than 10,000 units sold by quarter-end. Inquiries, preorders and walk-ins are up several times in Rajasthan and UP, and Konarc Z demand is strong.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ASP rise driven by scooter buyers or motorcycle buyers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the buyers are still scooter buyers paying for better experience, quality and features, not motorcycle buyers. Stack Pro attach is high across the base.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 5.3% margin gain sustainable, and does the 2.7% SKU lever reverse?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 5.3% is broadly structural (price hikes, VAVE, cost reduction). The 2.7% SKU/incentive lever is more temporary and can be reopened if supply is tight or commodities stay high, but it is not one-off.

qa_highlights.question: How are dealer network expansion and experience-centre additions planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Fewer than 50 experience centres were added in the last two quarters as dealer expansion was held back. Expansion restarts around end of Q3 FY27, with noticeable numbers from Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Konarc variant rollout sequenced with mid variants first and entry variants later?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity constraints on 450 and Rizta changed the plan. SR2 and SR3 launched first, SR1 is due by Q4 once Aurangabad capacity is available, and Z comes later. Geographic rollout started in the North.

risks_watch: Commodity costs (aluminium, copper, plastics, memory) have stayed elevated for longer than expected; management says Q3 is unlikely to be worse than Q2, but the outlook is volatile.
The 2.7pp SKU and incentive lever is temporary and may reverse if supply eases, which could weigh on gross margin.

Capacity ramp risk: AURIC Phase 1 takes about two quarters to ramp, and the 12,000 units/month add-on is due by Q2 FY28; demand is 50,000-60,000 units/month against 77,000 installed capacity after Hosur and AURIC.
Konarc ramp and attach-rate uncertainty: early Konarc attach rates are strong, but its mix is less South-heavy, and management wants at least two quarters of data.
PAT is positive for the first time but management says it can fluctuate; PAT is not the near-term focus.
Dealer network expansion has been slowed; it restarts around end of Q3 FY27, so store additions and reach may lag demand.
Electric motorcycle timeline is not guided.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, capacity and margin recovery, with clear caveats: management called commodity costs a "bad news" item that has lasted longer than expected and said the current PAT is not the main focus. Management was reluctant to give forward figures, deferring Konarc attach rates, AURIC ramp timing and motorcycle timelines.
